title: Annotatio VI §.IV: Augustine’s own glosses — sacrament / Eucharist / panem Domini not Dominum
pass_a_gloss: When what he here calls body, or flesh and blood of Christ, elsewhere in a not unlike sense he exposits — in Tract. on John 27 he calls flesh of Christ and blood of Christ in the sacrament; in John 26 and to Januarius’s Inquiries ch. 3 Sacrament of body and blood; On Ecclesiastical Dogmas ch. 53 Eucharist; and what he also says of Judas with the remaining Apostles in Psalm 10 he interprets as the Eucharist first confected (John 12); and against the Donatists post Coll. ch. 6 bread; and in Tract. on John 59 bread of the Lord, not bread the Lord; in Psalm 3 figure of his Body; against Adamantius ch. 12 sign of his Body; on the Lord’s word according to Matthew Serm. 11 Sacrament of Flesh and Blood first confected; on Luke serm. 33 the Supper consecrated by his own hands.
pass_b_english: What Augustine calls body (or flesh and blood) he elsewhere glosses as flesh and blood in the sacrament, as sacrament of body and blood, as Eucharist.

Of Judas with the Apostles he means the Eucharist first made — bread, bread of the Lord not bread the Lord, figure and sign of his body, the sacrament first confected, the supper consecrated by his hands.
source_text: Quum, quod corpus, sive carnem & sanguinem Christi hic dicit, alibi, in non dissimili sententia, exponens, in Joan. tract. 27. appellat carnem Christi, & sanguinem Christi in sacramento, in Johan. 26. & ad Inquisit. Januarii cap. 3. Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis, de Eccles. Dogmat. cap. 53. Eucharistiam: & quod etiam de Juda quoque, unáque reliquis Apostolis, dicit in Psal. 10. interpretatur Eucharistiam primùm confectam in Johan. cap. 12. & contra Donat. post. Coll. cap. 6. panem, & in Johan. tract. 59. panem Domini, non panem Dominum, in Psal. 3. Corporis sui figuram, contra Adamant. cap. 12. Corporis sui signum, de verbo Domini secundum Matth. Serm. 11. Sacramentum Carnis & Sanguinis primùm confectum, de verbo Domini secundum Lucam. serm. 33. Cœnam manibus suis consecratam.
